subject: Re: Helion Health — clarification on controller vs processor for DSR bulk erase
messages:
From: Paul Smith <paul.smith@helionhealth.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@helionhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Bulk erase request and controller vs processor clarification

Hi Tessa,

We’re running a routine privacy sweep at Helion and have a batch of patient identifiers stored in logs and training caches that we need to have removed across vendors. Attached is a PDF with the record IDs and requested deletion scope.

Two quick asks:
- Can you confirm whether Redwood is acting as controller or processor for data stored in our Dedicated cluster (we’ve onboarded under a dedicated commitment)?
- If Redwood is a processor, what evidence/process and timeline do you need for a bulk erase (we’re expecting ~5k records).

We’d also appreciate any exported evidence (audit logs, deletion confirmation manifest) and whether you can supply SIG/CIS excerpts showing deletion handling. This is time-sensitive for our compliance window (targeting completion by 2027-03-18).

Thanks,
Paul
Security & Privacy Ops
Helion Health
(Attachment: helion_dsr_request.pdf)

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Paul Smith <paul.smith@helionhealth.com>
Cc: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@helionhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bulk erase request and controller vs processor clarification

Paul — thanks for the details and the PDF. I’ve looped in Neha (privacy), Vivek (legal) and Olga (security) to confirm the classification and the evidence we can provide.

Preliminary answers: we typically act as processor for customer data in Dedicated (customer-controlled keys and network), but there are edge cases (custom ingestion where Redwood enriches logs) that need a quick review. We’ll confirm the role and provide a proposed timeline and list of deliverables by EOD tomorrow.

Requested next steps from our side:
- Internal triage to confirm data location and whether any transforms occurred.
- If processor: produce deletion manifest (IDs, timestamps), audit log slice, and SIG excerpt where deletion controls are documented.
- If controller: we’ll flag required approvals and recommend a jointly agreed plan.

I’ll follow up shortly — apologies for the quick turnaround ask from your compliance window.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redwood_dsr_process_map.pdf)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 13:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Bulk erase request and controller vs processor clarification

Tessa — quick notes from privacy side after a first-pass:
- Dedicated clusters: default relationship is processor. Customer controls network, keys (KMIP) and config.
- Exceptions: if Redwood performed model retraining using Helion-provided PII without a clear written instruction or if we derived new identifiers and used them outside customer boundary, we may have controller-like obligations.

Action items for us:
1) Engineering: confirm whether any Helion records were used in training corpora or offline feature stores (Vivek, can you ask infra?)
2) Security: prepare SIG CAIQ excerpts showing deletion and retention controls we can share (Olga)
3) Ops: estimate bulk delete runtime for 5k records from live KV caches + logs (engineering ops)

I can draft a processor confirmation letter for Helion once we have the infra check. If there’s any doubt we should surface that to Helion and propose a joint verification window.

-Neha
Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Bulk erase request and controller vs processor clarification

Quick update from infra: the dataset referenced in helion_dsr_request.pdf is present in the dedicated tenant logs and in a short-term KV cache used by the inference runtime; there is no evidence of full-model retraining with those PII fields. Engineering Ops reports:
- Logs: deletions are straightforward — we can scrub the entries and produce a deletion manifest with timestamps. Estimated completion: 48 hours after approval.
- KV cache: eviction + explicit purge required; we can provide a manifest and audit log entries. Estimated completion: 72 hours after approval because we need a rolling purge to respect latency SLOs.

Given this, Neha, I think processor classification is appropriate. Olga — can you confirm which SIG/CAIQ references we can share (redacted) and whether we need an NDA addendum for certain excerpts?

—Vivek

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 11:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Bulk erase request and controller vs processor clarification

We can share the following artifacts for processor evidence (redacted as needed):
- Excerpt from CAIQ: sections I-1 (data retention) and I-4 (data destruction) — can be redacted for internal telemetry names.
- Deletion handling section from our SOC 2 policy (PDF excerpt).
- Example deletion manifest template and an audit-log slice (note: full logs require Helion authorization to export).

No NDA addendum required for the CAIQ/SOC excerpts; for raw logs export we need explicit written consent from Helion (privacy policy inbound request OK). I’ve attached a short excerpt (sig_evidence_excerpt.pdf) with the lines we can ship immediately.

Olga
Director, Security Compliance
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: sig_evidence_excerpt.pdf)

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Paul Smith <paul.smith@helionhealth.com>
Cc: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@helionhealth.com>, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Bulk erase request and controller vs processor clarification

Paul — short update and proposed plan to meet your 2027-03-18 window:

1) Role: Redwood confirms we are acting as processor for the requested dataset in the Dedicated tenant.
2) Timeline: we can complete log scrubs and KV purge within 72 hours once Helion approves the scope and provides explicit written consent to export the deleted-log slice (Helion asked for this in their initial PDF). Target completion if approved: 2027-03-18.
3) Deliverables: deletion manifest (CSV), audit-log slice (redacted) and CAIQ/SOC excerpts documenting deletion controls.

Next steps for Helion: please reply with written consent to (a) proceed with the purge and (b) allow redwood to export the audit slice to the secure drive link in the related_links above. Once we have that, Ops will schedule the rolling purge and share the manifest as attachments.

Thanks — we’ll stand by to begin as soon as you confirm.

Best regards,
Tessa Morgan
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0199
(Attachments: redwood_dsr_process_map.pdf, sig_evidence_excerpt.pdf)
